tldr: MobileInject (Oct 16) framed prompt injection as a reasoning-to-action risk for MLLM-based mobile agents. Heads of Security (Oct 27) then proposed a defense: learned per-head attention gates that enforce instruction-data separation.
whats_new: SecPO (Oct 30) proposes adversarial training against prompt injection, positioned against Meta-SecAlign, the existing best-defended LLM.
why_it_matters: Prompt injection is a top agent threat, and the research is moving from attack evaluation toward defenses at the model level (attention gating, adversarial training).

status.detail: Three arXiv papers move from an attack benchmark to two model-level defenses; none is yet validated in production.

beats.headline: MobileInject evaluates injection against mobile agents
Heads of Security gates attention to separate instructions from data

open_questions: Do HoS or SecPO results hold against adaptive attackers outside their own evaluations?
Will either defense ship in an open-weight model or an agent framework?
take_for_builders: Treat these as research, not controls: keep least-privilege tool scopes and confirmation on agent actions, and rerun your own injection tests before relying on any model-level defense.
